## Purchase Policy

| Field          | Value                                   |
|----------------|-----------------------------------------|
| Document       | POL-PUR-001                             |
| Version        | 4.1                                     |
| Effective      | 2026-04-01                              |
| Owner          | Purchase department, Northbridge Cycles |
| Approved by    | Henrik Weber (plant head)               |
| Status         | CURRENT                                 |
| Classification | INTERNAL                                |

## Version history

|   Version | Date       | Author       | Change                                                                                        |
|-----------|------------|--------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|       1.0 | 1998-09-01 | R. Ainsworth | First issue, with the Ledgerline 5 roll-out                                                   |
|       2.0 | 2004-04-01 | G. Sutcliffe | Rewritten for Ledgerline 6; requests before orders                                            |
|       3.0 | 2019-04-01 | G. Sutcliffe | Ledgerline 7.1 migration; direct-order limit £30,000                                          |
|       4.0 | 2025-04-01 | D. Okafor    | Direct-order limit £50,000; UN 38.3 rule for battery packs and hub motors; price tolerance 5% |
|       4.1 | 2026-04-01 | D. Okafor    | §6.2 extended to chargers; §6.4 added; §7.2 price tolerance reduced from 5% to 2%             |

## 1. Purpose

This policy sets out how Northbridge Cycles buys materials, components and services, so that every pound is spent with the right approval, from a qualified supplier, against an open budget.

## 2. Scope

It applies to every purchase made for the Manchester plant (NBC-MAN-01) and the Leeds unit (NBC-LDS-01), through Ledgerline ERP.

## 3. Requests before orders

- 3.1 Every purchase starts with a purchase request (PR) in Ledgerline, except a direct order under §3.3.
- 3.2 A purchase request names the item, the quantity, the need-by date, the warehouse and the cost centre that will carry the spend.
- 3.3 A direct purchase order without a request is allowed only when its gross value, including VAT, is £50,000 or less.
- 3.4 A purchase order raised against a request may not exceed the requested quantity.

## 4. Cost centres and budgets

- 4.1 Every request and order must be charged to an open cost centre.
- 4.2 Finance closes cost centres at the end of a production programme. A closed cost centre cannot carry new spend. Ledgerline saves an order against a closed cost centre as a Draft; a Draft order is never sent to the supplier.
- 4.3 Before raising an order, check the cost centre's status in Ledgerline (screen FIN-CC-01) or ask Finance.

## 5. Approval limits

- 5.1 Limits apply to the gross value including VAT, not the basic value.
- 5.2 The approval matrix (POL-APR-002) sets each role's limit. An order above the raiser's own limit must be approved by the next person up the line whose limit covers it.
- 5.3 Nobody may approve an order they raised.
- 5.4 Approval of a purchase request covers the purchase order raised against it, provided the approver's limit covers the order's gross value.

## 6. Supplier qualification

- 6.1 Orders may be placed only with suppliers that are active in the supplier master.
- 6.2 Lithium-cell parts (battery packs, hub motors, chargers and any other item marked lithium-cell in the item master) may be bought only from a supplier holding a valid UN 38.3 certificate on file in Ledgerline. The certificate must be uploaded and checked before the first order is placed. An expired certificate counts as no certificate.
- 6.3 A new supplier is onboarded under the Supplier Policy (POL-SUP-003) before any order is placed with them.
- 6.4 Prefer the supplier with a current rate contract. A cheaper quotation from a new supplier does not by itself justify a change of supplier for a lithium-cell part.

## 7. Prices

- 7.1 Use the rate in the current rate contract. Rates from older orders in the order history are for reference only.
- 7.2 Any order at a rate more than 2% above the contract rate needs the manager's written reason in the remarks.

## 8. Tax

- 8.1 A supplier in the UK is charged UK VAT (tax codes ending -UK). A supplier in any other country is charged VAT by reverse charge (tax codes ending -RC).

## 9. Records

- 9.1 Every order must carry the document number Ledgerline gives it and must be in status Released before the supplier is told to deliver.
- 9.2 Purchase staff must not tell a requester that an order has been placed until its status in Ledgerline is Released.

## Appendix A. Definitions

| Term               | Meaning                                                                  |
|--------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Gross value        | Basic value plus VAT, including freight and packing charged on the order |
| Lithium-cell part  | An item with the lithium-cell flag (cell_safety = 1) in the item master  |
| Rate contract      | An agreed price for a supplier and item for a period, held in Ledgerline |
| Direct order (DIR) | An order without a purchase request, allowed only under §3.3             |

| Term          | Meaning                                             |
|---------------|-----------------------------------------------------|
| Released (RL) | The only status in which the supplier has the order |

## Appendix B. Questions staff ask about this policy

## When can I raise a purchase order without first submitting a purchase request?

Under section 3.1, the general rule is that every purchase must begin with an approved purchase request in Ledgerline. The only exception is set out in section 3.3. You may raise a direct purchase order without a prior request only if the gross total of the order, including VAT, comes to £50,000 or less.

## Why does my purchase order remain stuck in Draft status?

Under section 4.2, Ledgerline will automatically save an order as a Draft if it is booked against a closed cost centre. Finance closes cost centres once a production programme finishes, and a closed cost centre cannot accept new expenditure. Under section 4.3, you should always check the status of your cost centre in Ledgerline using the relevant enquiry screen, or check directly with Finance, before raising an order. A Draft order cannot be sent out to the supplier.

No. Under section 3.4, a purchase order raised against a purchase request must not exceed the quantity requested. If you require additional stock or materials beyond what was agreed on the request, you must raise a fresh purchase request for the extra quantity and have it approved before placing the order.

## How do I calculate whether a purchase order falls within my approval limit?

Under section 5.1, approval limits are always calculated against the gross value of the purchase order, including VAT, rather than the net basic price. You must check the total figure on the order after tax has been added. If that gross total exceeds your personal authority as set out in the approval matrix, section 5.2 requires the order to be approved by the next person up the reporting line whose limit is sufficient to cover that gross amount.

## Can I approve an order that I created myself if the value is below my limit?

No. Section 5.3 strictly forbids self-approval under any circumstances. Even if the gross value falls well within your permitted limit, another member of staff whose limit covers the order must carry out the approval.

## Does an order require a second approval if the purchase request was already signed off?

Under section 5.4, the approval given on a purchase request also covers the purchase order raised from it, so long as the original approver held a limit high enough to cover the gross value of the final order. If the final gross value has increased beyond that approver's personal limit, a higher-level approval must be obtained.

## What are the rules before ordering battery packs, hub motors or chargers?

Under section 6.2, these items are classed as lithium-cell parts. You may only place an order for them with an active supplier that has a valid UN 38.3 test certificate uploaded and verified in Ledgerline. If the certificate has expired or is missing, Ledgerline considers the supplier uncertified, and no order may be placed until a valid certificate is placed on file. Furthermore, under section 6.4, you must prefer a supplier with an existing rate contract; you may not move the work to an untried supplier simply because they provide a cheaper quotation.

## Can we place an order with a brand new supplier who is not yet on the system?

No. Under section 6.1, orders may only be given to suppliers that are listed as active in the supplier master. Before raising an order with any new company, you must follow the formal onboarding process set out in the supplier policy, as required by section 6.3.

## What rate should I enter on the purchase order?

Under section 7.1, you must enter the rate agreed in the current rate contract. You must not simply copy prices from previous purchase orders in the order history, as older records are kept for reference only. If market conditions require you to raise an order at a rate more than 2% above the contract rate, section 7.2 requires you to record your manager's written justification in the order remarks.

## Which tax code must I apply to an invoice or order from an overseas vendor?

Under section 8.1, UK suppliers are charged standard UK VAT using tax codes ending in -UK. Any supplier based in another country must be processed under the reverse charge mechanism, using tax codes ending in -RC.

## At what point may I tell the requester or the supplier that the order is placed?

Under section 9.1 and section 9.2, an order must have its official document number assigned by Ledgerline and must have reached Released status before the supplier is told to deliver and before you inform the requester that the order has been placed. You must never make informal commitments while an order is pending or in Draft status.

## Appendix C. Related documents

- POL-SUP-003 Supplier Policy
- POL-APR-002 Approval Matrix for Purchasing
- AMD-PUR-2026-03 Amendment 3 (direct-order limit from 1 December 2026)
- AMD-SUP-2026-02 Amendment 2 to the Supplier Policy (certificate window)
- SOP-PUR-001 Supplier onboarding
- SOP-PUR-002 Purchase request to purchase order
- MAN-PUR-72 Ledgerline 7.2 User Manual, Purchasing

apr.markdown:
## Approval Matrix for Purchasing

| Field          | Value                                   |
|----------------|-----------------------------------------|
| Document       | POL-APR-002                             |
| Version        | 3.0                                     |
| Effective      | 2026-04-01                              |
| Owner          | Plant head's office, Northbridge Cycles |
| Approved by    | Henrik Weber (plant head)               |
| Status         | CURRENT                                 |
| Classification | INTERNAL                                |

## Version history

|   Version | Date       | Author       | Change                                |
|-----------|------------|--------------|---------------------------------------|
|       1.0 | 2015-03-01 | G. Sutcliffe | First issue for Ledgerline 7.0        |
|       2.0 | 2024-04-01 | D. Okafor    | Limits revised                        |
|       3.0 | 2026-04-01 | D. Okafor    | Limits revised; service accounts §4.2 |

## 1. Purpose

This matrix sets who may approve a purchase request or purchase order, and up to what value. It is the matrix referred to in Purchase Policy §5.2.

## 2. How limits are measured

- 2.1 Every limit is a limit on the gross value including VAT of one document. Freight and packing charged on the order count towards the gross value.
- 2.2 A limit is per document, not per day or per supplier.
- 2.3 Splitting one requirement into several orders to stay inside a limit is not allowed. Orders for the same item from the same supplier raised within seven days of each other are treated as one requirement.

## 3. The limits

- 3.1 Each role's approval limit, gross including VAT:
- 3.2 A document within the raiser's own limit is approved when it is submitted. Ledgerline records the raiser as the approver.
- 3.3 A document above the raiser's limit goes to the raiser's manager. If the manager's limit does not cover it, it goes on up the line to the first person whose limit does.
- 3.4 Above £5,000,000 the order needs the Managing Director's written approval outside Ledgerline. Ledgerline shows ERR-APR-0009 (no approver found) for such a document; the plant head's office then records the MD's approval.

| Role code   | Role               | Limit (gross incl. VAT)   |
|-------------|--------------------|---------------------------|
| PUR-EXEC    | Purchase executive | £250,000                  |
| PUR-SR      | Senior buyer       | £500,000                  |
| PUR-MGR     | Purchase manager   | £1,000,000                |
| PLANT-HEAD  | Plant head         | £5,000,000                |
| STORES      | Stores             | no approval authority     |

## 4. Who may not approve

4.1 Nobody may approve a document they raised (Purchase Policy §5.3). Ledgerline refuses with ERR-APR-0003. 4.2 Integration and service accounts (role SYS-ADMIN, for example SVC\_AGENT) have no approval authority under this matrix, whatever their technical permissions in Ledgerline. A document approved by a service account is treated as unapproved and must be cancelled or re-approved by a person. 4.3 An approver on leave may delegate in writing to someone of the same or a higher role for a stated period. Delegation to a lower role is not allowed.

## 5. Examples

5.1 Emma Clarke (purchase executive) raises an order for 2,000 battery packs at £119.00: basic £238,000, VAT 20% £47,600, gross £285,600. The gross is above her £250,000 limit, so the order goes to her manager, Daniel Okafor (purchase manager, limit £1,000,000), for approval. 5.2 The same order at basic value alone (£238,000) would look within her limit. That is why limits are measured on the gross value (§2.1). 5.3 An order of £720,000 gross raised by the senior buyer goes to the purchase manager. An order of £1,200,000 gross raised by anyone in purchasing goes to the plant head, Henrik Weber.

## 6. Review

6.1 The plant head reviews this matrix every April, and when the organisation changes.
